category_title: Quiet fourth-grade student with learning disabilities who prefers working alone and struggles with task initiation
minimal_context: Tyrone is working on a narrative writing prompt about a day off from school during the morning block.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for our daily writing. Think about what you do on a day off from school. Now, write a story about a time when you had a day off from school.

STUDENT: (Sits quietly at his desk without being able to start writing, preferring to work alone in the noisy atmosphere.)

TUTOR: How is your writing going?

STUDENT: Great.

TUTOR: Okay, please continue working on your story.

STUDENT: (He writes, 'I would read a book . play vido games with my brother .' then stops. He sits quietly again, having trouble generating and articulating ideas, and gives up on writing a cohesive story.)

options.A: Provide a less frequent schedule of breaks intermittently throughout the daily morning writing block.
options.B: Introduce digital storytelling into the writing block, combining narration, visuals, and sound through technology.
options.C: Review Tyrone's behavior tracking sheet with him, having him count all positive and negative marks.
options.D: Implement relatively tight timelines for completing the daily writing prompt during the morning block.
